utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I just remind you, Admiral, of the affirmation you took at the commencement. It still applies.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jokic. I'm going to continue where I left off yesterday in asking you questions in your testimony. Yesterday when I asked you about the units which were in the formation of the 9th VPS at the Bay of Boka, you said that it was the 16th Border Detachment, a mixed division of battleship landing ships, and the 69th missile base, the PBO division of the 337th Naval Rear Base, the unit for reconnoitering and information. And before your departure, that there was the 472nd Motorised Brigade there as well, up until the 25th of September, 1991. Now, my question to you is this: Apart from the ones you enumerated within the composition of the 9th VPS, did you have any other military units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the staff units and the artillery units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me please which artillery units you actually had?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 107th Coastal Artillery Group, which included the stationary coastal batteries along the coast; and two mobile battalions of 85 millimetres and 130 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was that the 107th Coastal Artillery Group or was it the Divizion or Artillery Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The coastal artillery group, that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And is the abbreviation the 107th OAD, as it was called?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It was the 107th OAG, coastal artillery group, because a divizion or artillery battalion is not made up of the entrenched units which are not mobile. They cannot be mixed with the mobile batteries.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many cannons are there -- were there in that unit or battery, in the mobile ones?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 85 millimetre ones have six cannons and the 130 millimetre batteries also have six cannons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And what about the 140th PK OAD, what's that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 140th Mobile Coastal Artillery Divizion or Artillery Battalion was a unit that was there before the operations started, that is to say during peacetime. And it incorporated and encompassed -- well, I can't tell you exactly all the units it did encompass, but that was what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, in that particular unit, did they have 130-millimetre cannons, a battery of cannons, of that calibre?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The unit was established -- was made up of the 141st Coastal Group, which at one time was within the composition of the sector itself. And then that divizion or artillery battalion formed the brigade -- a brigade I think for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Within the composition of which brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Trebinje Brigade, the 472nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How long was it in that composition?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war. I don't know what period exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But in the period of October to December, it wasn't within the composition of the Trebinje Brigade, was it, 1991 of course?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact title, the name, it went by, that particular unit. But I do know the number of batteries, the number of cannons, that were in my sector and that were in the sector of the 472nd Brigade, I know that quite exactly, and I think that that is the substance, the essence of it all. Not whether it was the 140th PK OAD or some other title or name. Now, if you want to know the strength of my artillery and the brigade as well, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I asked you yesterday and you left out, you omitted, the artillery, that is why I am trying to help you complete this. What is the TOS or TOS, TOC perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: TOC?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical centre -- experimental centre which incorporated the missile training ground for tests and training. It was located at Prevlaka, and individual points were to be found in Konavle, the elevations towards Dubrovnik to the south facing Budva.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, what is this technical experimental centre, what did it have within its composition of the various devices, weapons, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had a mortar. I think it was 120-millimetre mortar, one of those; and a Howitzer, 105 millimetres that one was; it had a 130-millimetre cannon as well, I believe. So it was a unit that was subordinated to the General Staff, or rather, the military institute of the JNA. And the commander was Colonel Telebat. Miroslav was his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Upon arrival at the naval military sector at the 7th of October, to the end of December, 1991, did you have at your disposal any weapons from this unit and were you in command of them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I found that unit there when I arrived in Vitaljina, I believe. That is to the north of Prevlaka, and I found those two or three weapons there. And they were used by the barracks commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it a Howitzer of 120-millimetre calibre, the P-30 type?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite possibly it was. But generally speaking there were three weapons, one was a mortar, one was a cannon, a Howitzer 122 millimetre that we called Gvozdika [phoen], or the 105-type Howitzer. I don't know exactly. But I know there were three weapons there, three pieces, and they were used for exercises and testing. They were very high-precision weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, in that particular unit did you have the VBRs that are called Oganj and Plamen, multiple rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The technical centre did not have any of those multiple rocket launchers. And when it did its testing and experiments, they would be brought in from the unit itself, the unit engaged in the experiments. But I never saw those kinds of weapons at Prevlaka itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You have before you an order from the 2nd Operative Group. The order is for the return of the 472nd Motorised Brigade to its original unit that had been sent to the command of the VPS, and the 42nd Motorised Brigade. Can you tell us the content of that order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order regulating the return of the 472nd Brigade to within the sector's composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: From what date?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 25th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And what about the time? Was the time specified?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 25th of October at 11.00. I have never seen this order, although it is an authentic order. And I'm not challenging it at all. However, in the documents that I looked through belonging to the archives, it says that the brigade was subordinated to the -- on the 27th of October. And an order -- there's another order which states that on the 25th of October, I should report to the Trebinje command post with the commander with a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You saw that document, but this is another document actually from that same archive, and it specifically defines the day and date when the 472nd Motorised Brigade goes back to the original formation in order to engage in combat operations in the broader region around Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I've already said I don't challenge this document at Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. all. It has all the facets of an order of this kind and also a signature. All I'm saying is that the first order relating to the command of that brigade, the one I had, specified the 27th of October. That's why this is a little surprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us in greater detail what this means, when the command of the 2nd Operational Group says that the brigade goes back to its original unit. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the original command, the command which was in command and superior to the subordinated unit in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that that brigade was temporarily taken out from its original composition -- or rather, the 9th VPS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not the whole truth. That particular brigade, at my request to General Strugar saying that the brigade was for 25 days within the Dubrovnik siege and used the artillery very extensively, he said that this solution was only a temporary one, provisional one, and that he would be issuing an order for its further full deployment. That's the real truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Would you please answer my questions rather than expanding your answers, but we'll come to that in due course. We'll come to the date under which it was actually under your command. But the substance of the matter is this: That the brigade went back to its original formation, not as you have been persistently stating, that the brigade or individual parts of the brigade, the battalions, the 3rd and 4th Battalions, that they were only attached to you temporarily. The essence of this is that you were the original unit for that brigade. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This brigade, was it within its original units, the 9th VPS, also between 1983 and 1989?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That brigade, was it within the composition of its original unit, the 9th VPS, did it remain there until the 25th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Until the 16th of October, the 4th Battalion of that brigade remained within the composition of the 9th VPS while the rest of it was temporarily detached, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the first ten days. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like this document to be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be marked D43.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness P133. This is from the binder that has already been used during the examination-in-chief. More specifically, tab 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is a photocopy of the personal file of Vladimir Kovacevic. May I ask you to go straight to page 4, where we have a record of his active military service. That's the title just above the table that is shown on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English translation, it is also page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please have a look and tell me, line 5 of the document, line 6, looking from above down. The 6th box. It says that: "Vladimir Kovacevic is hereby transferred to the garrison of the VPS, the Trebinje garrison." Whereas up to that point, he had been in the reserve officer school in Bileca.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was he then transferred on the 27th of July, 1989, to the military naval district?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The next box just underneath this one, it says that he's being transferred outside the garrison for purposes of his service -- to serve as company commander with the 472nd Brigade of the navy's infantry, marked as B; naval infantry battalion, marked as A; the 9th VPS; Trebinje garrison. This order is dated the 30th of August, 1989, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's something here that was crossed out. This is not the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The far right you have the 30th of August 1989, and then added in handwriting that he took up duties on 2nd of August, 1990?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the next box just underneath -- you have looked at the previous box, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But what I see in the next box is that he took up his duties on the 12th of September. And just before it is stated that he took up his duties on the 2nd of October, the same year. But here we're talking about 1989, and there what I see is 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But which duty was it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Motorised Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That's right. Whereas in the previous box he was assigned to the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as the commander of the 3rd Company. I think there's a slight mistake there. I'm not sure I understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very well at all because this is simply inaccurate. In the previous box it says that he assumed his duties as commander of the 3rd Company in the 1st Battalion, whereas in the next box it says acting commander of the 3rd Company within the battalion. But this simply can't be; this makes no sense at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it makes any sense or not, but this is part of his personal file. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you will agree that it makes no sense at all that he would have been assigned as duty company commander, and then a year later -- well, I don't know, there must be a mistake here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on, please, the box just underneath, commander of the 3rd Motorised Brigade of the 472nd Motorised Battalion [as interpreted]. The unit is part of the 9th VPS of the military naval district, Trebinje Garrison. To the right, at the far right, the date is the 10th of May, 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. None of it's correct, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The transcript, page 9, line 18, reads: "3rd Motorised Brigade of the 472nd Motorised Battalion." It should be reversed, battalion, brigade. 3rd Motorised Battalion of the 472nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the table it is stated there very accurately, the commander of the 3rd Motorised Company of the Motorised Battalion A.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the next box of the 472nd Motorised Brigade marked as R, 9th VPS military naval district VPO, Trebinje Garrison. The unit is marked in this way as well as the location of the garrison. If you look at the next box in this table, the second box from left to right, where it states where he's serving, in which unit, in which institution, and in which garrison.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow, if all these three boxes, Captain Kovacevic is assuming his duties as company commander. This is quite simply impossible. Between 1989 and 1991, he's three times assigned the same duty as company commander. How can that be possible? If you look at this box you just read out to me and the one before that --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: At first, he was acting commander and then he was company commander.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but before that he was company commander, not acting company commander. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said that was crossed out.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, please, if you will allow, only the date was crossed out. I cannot accept your position. I think we must subject this to expert analysis. This is an obvious error.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let's try again. Underneath the text, this box where it says that he is being transferred to your garrison for purposes of service, the first box on the left it says: "Commander of the 3rd Company of the naval infantry in the 1st Battalion of the naval company A." That's the 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The box just underneath: "Acting commander of the 3rd Motorised Brigade of the motorised battalion." Doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How come he's acting commander now whereas before he was commander --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I would just like to point out on page 11 line 7 it should read 3rd Motorised Company of the motorised battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many battalions does a brigade have?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is only about one battalion. It says under A in peacetime only one battalion, three companies, and every company builds up to a battalion, at least while I was commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that a brigade has three companies that makes up a battalion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in peacetime. We're talking about peacetime, but each company builds up to a battalion in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please tell me how many battalions are there that are part of the 472nd Motorised

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In wartime, in war formation, four. In peacetime, there's only one. That's how it was while I was commander there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can an officer go from one battalion to another, pursuant to an order, of course?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please look at the far right, the boxes that are at the far right. In all three cases is it correct that where it says: "Instruction or order regulating the state of affairs," each and every time this is an order issued by the command of the military naval district, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably -- no. This can't be the military naval district. This is personnel administration. When he left Bileca, camp B. Then underneath you have the command of the military naval district, yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Personnel administration SSNO is transferring him from the infantry unit in Bileca to the Trebinje garrison to serve with the military naval district, and his further status in the military naval district is regulated by orders from the commander of the military naval district. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does this confirm the fact that the 472nd Brigade was with its original formation of the 9th Military Naval Sector, or rather, 9th Military Naval District?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as of the 5th of May -- as of the 10th of May. That's the 10th of May is the last date. The 10th of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This is precisely the period of time under discussion, isn't it? That's how it was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 10th of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What does that mean, the 10th of May, 1991? What does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the point he was appointed commander, company commander with the motorised battalion formation A.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That's how it remained until the commencement of the Dubrovnik operation in October and until Commander Ekrem Devlic was wounded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not how it was. I believe he was appointed, I'm not sure when, as deputy commander of the battalion first.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can't see that anywhere. It's not stated specifically in this order. It was probably this way, the way it reads here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of February, 1992, did he switch from the military naval district to the 13th Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. This is the first time I see this document, but if I look at it I see that this indeed is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So up to that point, he had been with the military naval district with the 472nd Brigade, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, but you can't really see it from this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Oh, this does in fact indicate that. It says: "Pursuant to an order of the SSNO 2/35, dated the 19th of February, 1992, he is hereby transferred to the 13th Corps." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, but this is the first time I realise that he was ever part of that corps. I'm not sure if he was, as a matter of fact, or whether this is just a fictitious transfer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that this document tendered into evidence by the Office of the Prosecutor during the examination-in-chief is a fabricated document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I'm saying. I'm just saying that I don't know it for a fact that he was part of that formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Jokic, maybe it is not given to you to know everything there is to know.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I would tend to agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll no longer be requiring this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So we have now determined the date as the 17th of October, or rather, the 16th of October as the final date until which the 4th Battalion remained in the composition of the 9th VPS. Furthermore, we determined --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: That's not the evidence. That date is not the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What do you say it should be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The -- could he ask the witness to correct it, Your Honour? That's not what the witness said earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand this may be a bit complex, but I've have three answers from the witness to the effect that the 4th Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade until as late as the 16th of October remained part of the 9th VPS. I believe we can have the witness confirm this yet again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... For the witness to answer this, not for counsel to testify consistently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has answered this question three times already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, if you want to put to the witness that it is established by his evidence that there was a certain date, you have a problem, because his evidence does not at the moment identify such a date. There is more than one possible date. So if you want to start with the proposition that there is a clear date, you'll have to pursue that question with the witness further. Alternatively, leave out a reference to the date and proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just have a minute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to proceed, and my Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. colleague is going to find this. Because I'm sure that I did get an answer to that question today.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let us repeat this once again. The Trebinje Brigade, the 472nd Motorised Brigade, from the 25th of October until the 20th of November, 1991, was it within the 9th VPS Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on page 7, in line 4, you can check this for yourselves, I asked today whether the 4th Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade until the 16th of October was within the 9th VPS, Military Naval Sector. So my learned friend can check this in the transcript as well. And I would kindly ask her to follow the proceedings more carefully.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your -- could we go to the response then, please, for page 7. Excuse me, can I just check that on the other computer because I can't see it on this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. The question on that page -- the response was: "A. Until -- yes, for the first ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Until the 16th of October, the 4th Battalion of that brigade remained in the composition of the 9th VPS while the rest of it was temporarily detached, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the first ten days -- first days of October."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Or the first ten days from the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can we ask to have the witness clarify it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the position, Mr. Rodic, clearly is that there is some uncertainty where you felt there was certainty. If you want to be sure about certainty, I think you need to put the matter again to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Mr. Jokic, but let me ask you yet again. Is it correct that the 4th Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade until the 16th of October was within the 9th VPS, Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, last time, yesterday, I also said that when I came and when I took up my duties, this 4th Battalion had been taken out of combat and it was on leave in Igalo. And then orders followed, I think on the 10th, that the battalion should be reassigned to the brigade. I don't know exactly which date this was. It was not in combat, so they were taken from leave. It was some date around the 10th or after the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: My question was whether it was within the 9th VPS, whether it was subordinated to you until the 16th of October, 1991, not whether it was in combat or whether it was on leave. Could you tell me yes or no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The answer was that it was on a date of which the witness is not certain, around the 10th or after the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We'll proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the 472nd Motorised Brigade on the 20th of November left the 9th VPS, that it was still within the 9th VPS -- or rather, that the 3rd Battalion of that brigade was still within the 9th VPS all the way up to the end of December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That battalion was temporarily subordinated to the 9th VPS; whereas, the original brigade that you were talking about, the 472nd, it never returned within the ranks of the 9th VPS. It was never reassigned to the 9th VPS.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to answer my questions briefly. Do not expound to that extent, please. Did the 3rd Battalion remain under you temporarily or did it remain within its original brigade and was the rest of the brigade temporarily assigned to another task, to another unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion was subordinated to the 9th Sector temporarily, while the brigade went to carry out its tasks - and it says so in the order - the 472nd Brigade left one of its battalions temporarily within the 9th Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: We looked at a document, D43, earlier on, and that was the command of the 2nd Operational Group, that the 472nd Motorised Brigade should return to its original ranks, its original establishment. Was that the order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but now we're talking about the 21st of November, when the brigade left the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For this battalion, is the brigade its original unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For the brigade, is the 9th Military Naval Sector its original unit or establishment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the battalion -- or rather, the sector is not the original unit of the battalion. There is a major difference involved there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That is your answer. Thank you. Can you tell me whether the 2nd Operational Group is a temporary organisation which never existed before with that kind of establishment?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the 2nd Operational Group as a temporary establishment never had an area of responsibility within which the commander was compelled to carry out operations?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. The 2nd Operational Group, when it was established and when it was given its orders -- or rather, its directives, it also got its area of responsibility. And this area of responsibility included the border between Croatia and Montenegro all the way to the Neretva River. That was its area of responsibility. It was a wartime unit and a war zone. It is not a peacetime unit, or rather, command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was this zone then all the way up to Mostar? Did it include Mostar in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did. I think it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many garrisons and which garrisons then were under the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the 2nd Operational Group were all the garrisons that the 9th sector had as the subordinate command. Then the garrisons that the brigade had, the 472nd Brigade, and those garrisons of the 37th and 2nd Corps that were subordinated to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Where's the 37th Corps from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was temporarily detached to that zone of operations and subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group, and it came from Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Where is Uzice?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In which military district? Which military district did the 37th Corps from Uzice belong to?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which military district. I think it belonged to the 3rd Military District. I'm not sure. It was not within my sphere of interest. I do not have this knowledge, but I think it was the 3rd District. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: According to that analogy, are you claiming that the command of the 2nd Operational Group had within it the Uzice garrison as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I claim is that it includes all the garrisons in the zone of operations. We do not understand each other at all. I have already explained what a zone of operations is in wartime. This is the area between the border of Montenegro and Croatia, Debeli Brijeg, Prevlaka, including Mostar, the Neretva valley, and the units that were subordinated to the 2nd Operational Group that was perhaps the Nevesinje-Gacko line. I think that would be right answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Zone of operations and area of responsibility, are they one in the same thing in military terminology?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that most of the soldiers from the 2nd Operational Group belonged to the reservists and volunteers, because the JNA was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. primarily manned from the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these soldiers, reservists, were called up for mobilisation for a military exercise? They were not called up to go to war because a state of war had not been declared?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it precisely for that reason that later on a decision was made to the effect that units would be used for 45 days, and then they would go on leave, or rather, the soldiers comprising those units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there was such a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it an additional problem that there weren't enough -- there wasn't enough trained personnel?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a broader problem. It's not a question of a shortage. It is a question of speedy mobilisation and manning with inadequate personnel and a lack of training before bringing them into combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So what is correct is that the reservists were not sufficiently trained, or that as a matter of fact they were untrained for the situation that they found themselves in in the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does all of that together constitute an objective set of circumstances which considerably aggravate efficient command, irrespective of the rank of commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the doctrine of command of the JNA, tasks are first issued to subordinate units -- or rather, their commanders, and in this way each commander down the entire chain of command issues orders to commanders and officers subordinated to him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this commander who issues orders first to units directly subordinated to him first receives this task from his superior officer, then elaborates on that and sends it down the chain. That is the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: According to the doctrine of command, did the JNA prefer a centralised command system, which implied the absence of initiative?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That principle in the JNA was - how shall I put it? - very much emphasised, although initiative as such was okayed in reasonable limits, if it contributes to the overall task and assignment of the higher-up unit, if its success will contribute to the success -- the overall success of the unit above it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it correct that in October 1991 on one occasion you said that "Dubrovnik is a Croatian town, and after this operation of ours it will continue to be a Croatian town, but that nobody dared publicise that?"

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Ask when and what context. Focus on where the alleged quote may have come from. It's unfair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it is an extremely wide-ranging question, Mr. Rodic. I think it reasonable that you should be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And I should like to remind my learned colleague that this is to be found in several interviews which Mr. Jokic gave to the Prosecution and I assume --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... for Ms. Somers, it is a matter for the fairness of the question you put to the witness. So if you want to identify some past statement of his, have him confirm that he made it, identify it with sufficient certainty to give the witness a chance of remembering it and identifying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The most recent place you stated this, linked to the media, the public information media, is the interview in the magazine Nin dated the 16th of November, 1991. I misspoke. 2001. I apologize. Is that true? Is that the latest instance?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If you put the interview to the individual, and I would like to point out that Mr. Rodic said October, 1991. Perhaps the interview is available and the witness can take a look at what he allegedly said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you got it to hand, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour, but I'm going to go into that matter in due course a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In an interview to the magazine Nin, let's be quite precise here. I think it was the 16th of November, 2001. Yes, the 16th of November, 2001. It was my mistake if I said October 2001. Did you give an interview to the magazine Nin?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I could have given an interview because on the 16th of November I was in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in this weekly magazine Nin and it's issue of the 16th of November, 2001, did an interview of yours come out, was it published?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I don't know, because on the 12th of November I gave myself up voluntarily to The Hague. And three and a half months later, I returned to the country. And if you give me a copy to see -- to have a look, I'll will be happy to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But you say you don't know about that, you don't know whether the interview was published --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection. This is twisting the witness's words. It's confusing the witness. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't think it's confusing the witness, but it may not be accurately putting the witness's words to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If perhaps we could look at the alleged interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're wasting a lot of time at the moment, Mr. Rodic, on what really is a minor aside. The witness doesn't presently remember the interview, if I understand his evidence. If you want him to remember it right now, I would suggest he should be shown the publication to ask whether that is a publication resulting from an interview he gave. If not, and you want to come back to that later, just move on and come back to it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will of course show the interview to the witness in due course, but I have reason for which I wanted to clarify this point, whether he knows that the interview was indeed published on the 16th of November, 2001. And I think my question is well-founded. All I'm interested in is to hear from him whether he knows that the interview was published in the issue of the 16th of November, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the present effective of his evidence is that without being reminded of the article, he doesn't remember giving such an interview because he was in The Hague at that time of publication.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you give an interview at all to the weekly magazine Nin in October 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, but I'm not quite sure. I gave two interviews to the Vecernje Novosti paper, I think to Vreme as well. I'm not sure about the Nin magazine, possibly. Possibly, I did. But I would have to check that out and see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Just one more question in that regard, please. The interview from the Nin magazine, was it ever shown to you by the Prosecution and did you state your views about it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have remembered. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an interview. I don't know when.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on and we'll come back to that interview. Did you ever advocate the formation of a Dubrovnik republic -- or rather, did you come out in favour of stating that Dubrovnik should be outside the borders of the Republic of Croatia? Just briefly, please, because I am afraid we're losing a lot of time. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Now, do you know Nikola Samardzic, who at the time in 1991 was the minister of foreign affairs of Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met him while he was the director of the Kotorska Providba company, the maritime company.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In this period when you met him and he was the director of Jugo-okeanija, was that the period you were the commander of the 9th VPS, from 1983 to 1989?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you know him well during that period, before the war, while you were commander in the Bay of Kotor? Did you visit one another? Would you see each other?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. He attended naval ceremonies in Kumbor several times. I don't really know whether I was there myself -- or rather, whether I was in that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, during the Dubrovnik operation, did you happen to see him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. As far as I remember, no. There was no reason or need.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you have contacts with him over the phone during that period of time perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember having had a telephone conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now, the next period, October/December 1991, while you were commander of the 9th VPS, did he ever ring you up, Nikola Samardzic, over the phone? And if he did phone you, did you ask him whether a Dubrovnik republic was something that was feasible?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It never entered my mind; it never occurred to me to ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you at odds at all with Nikola Samardzic? Have you had an argument?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And was there ever a situation in which Nikola Samardzic would call you up on the phone and that General Strugar -- when General Strugar was sitting next to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that situation is highly unlikely and almost impossible. How could he ring me up on the phone with a general sitting next to me who was my superior? How could that have ever happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Let me move on. In Dubrovnik -- or rather, Tivat and then Dubrovnik on the 29th of October, did a group of ambassadors come to visit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Now let me ask you this: With respect to this visit by the ambassadors to Dubrovnik, ambassadors who arrived in Tivat first in October 1991, were you contacted by the minister, Nikola Samardzic, and he was the minister of foreign affairs of the Republic of Montenegro, Nikola Samardzic was his name, or the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody contacted me, either the General Staff or Nikola Samardzic. And what's Samardzic got to do with that visit?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, a Nikola Samardzic testified to that effect before this Honourable Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Objection. Putting the testimony of another witness in this regard is not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is a justified observation, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know which the assignments of the 2nd Operational Group were and the goals of the operation itself during that period of time, the material time, that is to say, October to December 1991 or a little later?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can tell you the assignments with respect to my knowledge of the operation and after preparing my defence, because when I got to the battlefield, I didn't learn about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, tell us please what they were.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Operational Group had as its task and assignment, pursuant to a directive from the General Staff, to deblock the Prevlaka barracks, to take control of Kupari, to block the town of Dubrovnik from land and sea, and to reach the Neretva region, and to act jointly with the forces that from the Mostar region were operational towards Ploce. In the primary assignment -- or rather, the objective, the prime objective, was to act together with the forces along the Mostar/Split axis. However, this idea was given up fairly earlier on, because there was not sufficient manpower to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. According to that directive from the General Staff - and I'll try and remind you of the assignments and objectives of the 2nd Operational Group - was one of the tasks and assignments, pursuant to the directive, that the main forces along the Ljubinja/Zavala/Slano axis and then the village of Ljubovo, Ivanjica, Cibaci, and Grab, Dubravka, Molunat, with auxiliary forces and reinforcements to secure the facilities around the Mostar airport and the Neretva River valley with the aim of breaking the forces along the axis of attack and to emerge to the Adriatic coast to cut off the Adriatic highway at several sections in the Slano/Prevlaka section and to block by land Dubrovnik from the land and from the sea as well as the airport of Cilipi and to make it impossible for the enemy to perform its manoeuvres. And then by securing the Ploce axis, to destroy and disarm the enemy forces in the surrounding areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this is being read from a particular document, can it be identified so that it does not become the testimony of Mr. Rodic. If there is some source to check it off again, otherwise it is a lecture by Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the case, Mr. Rodic, that you're putting a quotation to the witness from a document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am basing this question on a document as well as other documents and all the information that the Defence team has gathered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be allowed to say something, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has been quoted from a directive on the attack that was part of the Dubrovnik operation, the commencement of the operation on the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So the objectives that I set out here are these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, you're still dealing with my concern. If you're quoting from a document such as that, the way to do it is to put the document to the witness if you want him to confirm what you are saying. It needs to be a document that can be identified by the Chamber, if it needs to, at a later date. It needs to be a document that can be verified by the Prosecution. It needs to be something which the witness can consider and decide whether it is what you are saying or not. Especially when you're purporting to quote such an extensive quotation from a document. It happens in this particular case. The document seems to be one very familiar to the witness, and he was able to give an answer. That would be unusual, and it will -- while it may have been something he could deal with, it still leaves the Chamber and the Prosecution without a means of identification and verification. So if you could identify the document now for the record and remember that in future, we'd be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do have the document in my possession, but there's no English translation of that document. So if that doesn't pose a problem, I'm quite willing to offer this document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we ask that we have the document before in whatever language it's available so that we can follow with some degree of understanding. Until we've had a chance, and perhaps the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Chamber has the same opportunity, we can avoid more questions on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Fortunately, Mr. Rodic, there will be a break quite soon so you can make copies if you haven't copies ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any copies available now, but I can make some during the break, Your Honour. That's no problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, can you please tell me, if you know, who took the decision to start the operation in the direction of Dubrovnik -- on Dubrovnik and further on. Who took the decision for the 2nd Operational Group to move towards Dubrovnik and further on to the Neretva River and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their command. The General Staff, as the supreme staff of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have an interpretation problem here. The witness said: "The supreme command." Whereas, on the transcript we see "their command," which are two very different things, as we all know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, when you came to the 9th VPS, Military Naval Sector, were you familiarised with the previous operations carried out by the National Guards Corps near the Prevlaka area or in Konavli, operations carried out against military convoys that were en route from Boka to Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was familiarised.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who told you about this.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first to talk about it was the chief of staff, Zec, but other officers spoke about it, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers who were wounded during those attacks?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether there was anyone who was wounded at Prevlaka, but I don't think there were many casualties in terms of people being killed or wounded. I think the main thing was those acts of provocation against the barracks at Prevlaka, the military vehicles and convoys en route from Boka to Trebinje being checked, as well as the taking of the military holiday resort of Kupari.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please specify the period of time in which this was happening. Did they give you a specific period of time for these things?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before the 1st of October, 1991, August and September.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this may be a convenient time for us to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did we secure copies of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have secured copies, and I will now have them distributed, if we can have the usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, we don't have the English translation of this document, not for the time being anyway. Before the break, I asked a number of questions in relation to the objectives and tasks of the 2nd Operational Group. Therefore, I would now like to ask you for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the OTP. Since this document is in Serbian language, can we now please go through it. I will ask you questions, and if then you can please tell us what the document is about and confirm what I'm saying. This document in the upper left corner, you can see that it was issued by the command of the 2nd Operational Group on the 29th of September, 1991, at 1.00 p.m. at Kifino Selo. That is the location. That's probably where the command post of operational group was initially, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Just underneath, is this what it says: "Proposal for a decision on an offensive operation delivered to the command of the 2nd OG to the Chief of the General Staff of the armed forces of the SFRY, Lieutenant General Blagoje Adzic."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is the title of this document as follows: "Directive for attack OP. Number 2"?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the OTP, I would please like to ask you to read out item 1 and to say whether these are the objectives that you spoke about before the break.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1, I have decided as follows: From the present areas, to use the greater part of the forces and to start the attack along the main axis as follows: Ljubinja, Zavala, Slano, Ljubovo village, Ivanica, Cibaci and Grab, Dubravka, Molunat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. Do the interpreters have copies of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters don't really have copies but the B/C/S copy's on the ELMO, so we can see the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The auxiliary forces shall be used to secure facilities and the Mostar airport" - I don't think I - "and in the Neretva River valley with the following objective:" Yes, now I can hear you. Now it's all right. "With the following objective: With the support of the air force, artillery, and navy" -- I'm not receiving any interpretation now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, while you are speaking in Serbian, you are not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm not sure when the text is finished. That's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please just read on, but make sure to do it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. "By simultaneous and energetic action, crush the forces along the axis of the attack and reach the coast, cutting off the Adriatic highway, coastal road, at several places in the Slano/Prevlaka section. Block Dubrovnik from land and sea as well as the Cilipi airport and Prevlaka. Make it impossible for enemy forces to perform their manoeuvres. Then, by securing our own forces from the Ploce axis, start the destruction and disarming of the enemy forces that have been surrounded and be at the ready for further offensive operations into Western Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me the following: These objectives and tasks as given here for the entire operation in which the 2nd Operational Group was involved?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell me, based on this document, is it true that this operation was to be carried out in two separate stages and how was this set out?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. The first and second stage are set out in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us these specific tasks, as related to each of these two respective stages?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first stage is reach the sea coast and cut off the Adriatic highway, coastal road, the blocking of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you just please move on a bit faster.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The airport and the forces at Prevlaka, duration, two days. Second stage, completely crush, force to surrender and disarm enemy forces, and be at the ready for transferring offensive operations into West Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Duration of the operation, two to three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the next page, does it say anything about the operational disposition of the 2nd Operational Group, what it's supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The operational disposition as follows: Forces for the attack and blockade, forces for securing and defending facilities and the airport, forces for support and reserve. The attack to commence pursuant to a special order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you now please tell me about this initial stage of the operation along the Dubrovnik/Herzegovina axis. Which forces were at that point within the 2nd Operational Group and what were their respective tasks?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces of the 2nd Operational Group were as follows: The 37th Corps; the 472nd Brigade without the 4th Battalion and combat group 1; the 1st Brigade of the Territorial Defence from the 3rd Partisan Division; the 9th VPS with the 4th Battalion from the 472nd Brigade; and the Territorial Defence brigade from Titograd from the 21st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All these units that you have enumerated, do they all have special tasks assigned to them pursuant to this directive at the beginning of the operation, meaning tasks that were planned for them to carry out?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Every unit had its own task.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what the task of the 37th Corps was.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Here where the tasks are spelled out. Perhaps you don't have to read it. Perhaps you can read it to yourself and then tell us what the main elements of the task involved are.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the task of the 37th Corps is to use part of the forces along the Lubinje/Ravno/Slano axis to carry out an attack and to use another part of the forces to defend and take the airport of Mostar and other facilities in the Mostar area and in the Neretva River valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In that task, were they supposed to provide for the unhindered use of the airport, reach the coast, cut off the road, and reach the Bay of Slano, isolate Dubrovnik, and stop manoeuvres, and the intervention of the other side from the area of Ploce. Was that part of the task, too?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Inter alia, was part of the task to raid part of the forces of a mountain battalion in the area of Capljina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it the task of the 472nd Motorised Brigade under B to cut the road in the areas of Zaton and Cibaci, to block Dubrovnik and to cut off the airport of Cilipi. And then by securing the flanks, prevent any intervention towards Dubrovnik and start disarming and destroying enemy forces? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What about the 1st Brigade of the Territorial Defence from the 3rd Partisan Division? Have the task to get to the road and cut it off in the regions of Poljice and Mikulici, to block the airport of Cilipi from the eastern side, and establish direct contact with the 4th Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, and then start destroying enemy forces in the area of Gruda acting in concert with parts of the 9th Military Naval Sector in taking facility of Sutorina and Prevlaka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Although it is very inaccurate to say taking the facility of Sutorina and Prevlaka that were in our hands. Actually, these are parts of the territory where our forces were. So this is a flagrant mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Under D, the 9th Military Naval Sector with the 4th Battalion of the 472nd Motorised Brigade, was it supposed to destroy enemy forces and control Prevlaka and with naval forces to exercise control over exits -- entrances to the Bay of Boka Kotorska, to prevent manoeuvres, and enemy operations, and support by naval artillery the land forces, to be on the ready and carry out a landing from the sea when necessary?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: As for paragraph E of this directive, the brigade of Tijo Titograd did it establish a reserve in the area of 2nd Operational Group in the area of Trebinje, and was it supposed to be on the ready to be brought into the attack along the Trebinje/Dubrovnik and Trebinje/Cilipi axis?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that's what it's written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: On the last page of the document, paragraph 5. Does it regulate things as follows: That the command post of the 2nd Operational Group in the area of Kifino Selo and that the AKM, the forward command post of the operational group is in the area of Trebinje. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Under paragraph C, at the end of this directive, does it contain the following order: That the blockade of the port of Dubrovnik should take place when the attack begins, and in this way prevent access for all ships to the coast. And make it impossible to carry out -- make it impossible for all civilian and foreign ships to carry out an attack?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was this document compiled and signed by the commander of the 2nd Operational Group Lieutenant Colonel General Jevrem Cokic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the objectives and tasks of the 2nd Operational Group, and within it the tasks of the 9th Military Naval Sector?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I came to the theatre of war, I had not seen this directive or read it. Only the chief of staff told me that there was a directive, and that is a document in an envelope with a large number of other accompanying documents and maps. And he said something along the following lines: That it was not acted upon, rather, it was combat orders that were acted upon. I found this directive in the archives, and I read it. But in addition to this directive, there is yet another directive containing nine pages. The date, I think, was the 30th of September, 1991. It contains several details, but the two are similar in terms of their objectives, tasks, and the commands that are there to carry out the tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: That is precisely what I would like to ask you so that we clarify it. Since we see that this document is entitled "Proposed decision for an attack operation," and it is being submitted to the chief of General Staff of the armed forces of the SFRY, Colonel General Blagoje Adzic, does that mean that the General Staff reviews this directive, perhaps amends it in some ways, and then approves it only after that. Is that the procedure?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that mean then that the General Staff is the one that exercises control over the attainment of these objectives and implementation of these tasks involved in the operation for which it established a temporary military formation which is called the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The General Staff of the armed forces of the SFRY in the period that we are talking about, from October to December 1991 but later on as well, did it regulate certain situations through separate orders of their own in which it issued separate tasks to the 2nd Operational Group, those that they were supposed to implement?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it's supposed to be. I don't know what kind of documents the General Staff issued to the command of the 2nd Operational Group. Whether this was a new directive, whether these were orders, I don't know that. Because I never received this, of course. It was not for me to receive. And I didn't find any in the archives, this particular documentation of the General Staff. I didn't find it in the archives either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If you have not seen this, bearing in mind what we discussed previously, that the General Staff exercises control over the 2nd Operational Group and the entire operation, was the General Staff then supposed to follow the objectives and tasks during the operation and to regulate it, as you had put it, through orders or other documents? In principle, is that the way the General Staff was supposed to operate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it was supposed to operate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The tasks that the General Staff assigned to the 2nd Operational Group down the chain of command, were they taken further down the chain of command to subordinate commands, or rather, subordinate commanders from the 2nd Operational Group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand what you said -- or rather, that's not the procedure involved. The General Staff issues its document, its order, down to the command of the 2nd Operational Group. In that command, this document, this order, is elaborated, the situation is assessed, and a decision is made regarding further action. This document is then submitted as an order to the command of the 2nd -- of the command of the 2nd Operational Group further down to their subordinate commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In this specific case, they were?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the commands that we read out a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me one more thing in relation to this, as for a decision for further action, which is elaborated and adopted by the command of the 2nd Operational Group, is this adopted in accordance with orders received from the General Staff -- in accordance with orders and tasks received from the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have finished dealing with this document. I have finished examination in relation to this document, and I would like to tender it into evidence as a Defence exhibit. We will make an effort to provide an English translation as well, so we will submit that subsequently. But for the most part, we have dealt with the document through the witness and we've had it read out basically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic. The document will be received if we could ask that the translation be provided before the Easter break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll do our best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is marked D44.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic, before the break I asked you about when you came to the 9th Military Naval District to take over your duties. I asked you whether you were informed about the situation in the area of responsibility of the 9th Military Naval Sector and whether there were any persons, any soldiers, who were wounded in attacks by the MUP forces and the National Guards' Corps of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I have answered that I was aware of this and, if necessary, I can discuss it in greater detail. I do not remember any losses. Perhaps there were one or two persons who were wounded, but I don't remember more than that. This was at Prevlaka.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: During the operations that were carried out by your units and by other units under the command of the 2nd Operational Group, were there any soldiers of the other side that were taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. But for the most part these were people out of uniform and without weapons, as far as, except for one case near Molunat, where a few men were taken prisoner, as well as a 85-millimetre gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember the case that happened at Molunat, when that was, what period, timewise?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was before I arrived, between the 1st and 5th or 6th of October. But I do know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The people who were taken prisoner, if they had any health problems, for instance, if they had been wounded or injured in any way were they provided medical assistance at all, health assistant care?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. All the injured and wounded were evacuated to the Meljine hospital and treated there, just like all our other wounded men.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that no distinction was made between the two, that is to say wounded and injured members of the 2nd Operational Group and the members of the other side who were taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not make any difference or differentiate between them now with respect to treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you ever happen to visit any of the wounded in the military hospital at Meljine?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember two occasions. Once when a member of the Croatian defence was taken prisoner at Bosanka. His name was Damir Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, this man, Damir Kos, did he tell you where he was from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said he was from Koprivnica and that he had reported for duty as a volunteer at Mesic's vessel which led the convoy to Dubrovnik, and that he was issued weapons in Dubrovnik and deployed to the Bosanka facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wounded and taken prisoner there and transported to the Meljine hospital, where I questioned him about that whole incident, that is to say the case of the volunteers who made reinforcements for Dubrovnik on the 31st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, did he come to Dubrovnik as a volunteer on the "SLAVIJA" ship in the convoy led at the time by the Yugoslav state president, Stjepan Mesic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, you said that he was from the town of Koprivnica. So give us a rough estimate as to the distance from Koprivnica to Dubrovnik and tell us where Koprivnica is located. Give us the name of a larger town nearby.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG JOKIC [Resumed]
